title: State and behaviour that keep an invariant

blocks.text: An object's **fields** hold its state and its **methods** are its behaviour. The methods are what keep the state valid: here, no quantity is ever negative. The page also warns against **forgetting to initialise fields**: a field must hold a usable value from the moment the object exists, set at its declaration or in the constructor.

items: `add(String item, int quantity)` adds stock (`quantity` is positive);
`remove(String item, int quantity)` takes stock away. Removing more than is held throws `IllegalArgumentException`, and then nothing changes;
`quantityOf(String item)` returns the quantity held, `0` for an unknown item;
`items()` returns the names of the items held, sorted alphabetically. An item whose quantity reached `0` is not listed.

blocks.text:
inv = new Inventory()
inv.quantityOf("bolt")      -> 0
inv.add("bolt", 5); inv.remove("bolt", 2)
inv.quantityOf("bolt")      -> 3
inv.remove("bolt", 4)       -> IllegalArgumentException, still 3
inv.remove("bolt", 3); inv.items() -> []

cases.says: Adding and removing stock changes the quantities the inventory reports.
A brand-new inventory answers 0 for any item and lists no items, without an exception.
Removing more than is held throws IllegalArgumentException and leaves the quantity as it was.
An item whose quantity reaches 0 disappears from the listed items.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Every field holds a usable value from the moment the object exists, set at its declaration or in the constructor.
